notes: Identity verified internally from the supplied primary text: title Tracing Attention and the Activation Flow in Spoken Word Planning Using Eye Movements; author Ardi Roelofs; Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition, 2008, Vol. 34, No. 2, 353–368; DOI 10.1037/0278-7393.34.2.353. The supplied text contains a full journal article with methods, results, references and appendix, rather than an abstract or secondary report. No supplied PDF path; no rendering or acquisition performed. Study 3 is Experiment 3 of the identified primary article. The description names attention/activation flow and eye movements, and the locator is only p. 10 (printed p. 362). This identifies a study and page, but does not specify task, semantic versus phonological contrast, main effect versus interaction, or participant versus item analysis. The page reports multiple gaze-shift F tests and vocal-response tests; gaze-shift planned contrasts continue on p. 363. Even restricting to eye movements leaves multiple plausible tests. The printed test statistic is available for several candidates, but no unique correspondence is supported. No target was selected by row order or numeric matching.
